title: COMELEC logs 180,000 voter registrations, mostly first-timers
summary: The Commission on Elections (COMELEC) has recorded more than 180,000 voter registrations since reopening its registration period for the 2028 national and local elections on November 10, with most…

blocks.text: The Commission on Elections (COMELEC) has recorded more than 180,000 voter registrations since reopening its registration period for the 2028 national and local elections on November 10, with most applicants being young people who will be voting for the first time.

“Mula nung nakaraang Sabado at umabot na po sa mahigit 180,000 ang iba’t-ibang klase ng registrations ang tinanggap ng COMELEC at karamihan po dito ay galing sa ating mga kabataan na magiging first time voters kaya nga po,” COMELEC spokesperson John Rex Laudiangco said during the Bagong Pilipinas Ngayon public briefing.
(Since last Saturday, COMELEC has accepted more than 180,000 applications for various types of registration, most of them from young people who will be first-time voters.)

Laudiangco said the poll body expects to surpass its initial target of 3 million registrations, noting that it also expects applications from voters whose registrations were deactivated after failing to vote in two consecutive elections.
He encouraged eligible Filipinos to register, including young citizens who are not yet 18 but will reach voting age by May 8, 2028.
Those who wish to update their voter information, including their residence or surname, may also apply for registration.

Laudiangco said the COMELEC has also introduced the Special Register Anytime/Anywhere Program (SRAP), which will make registration more accessible through satellite registration sites in public places such as malls, universities and government offices.
The list of SRAP registration sites will be posted on the COMELEC website and Facebook page, he said.
Meanwhile, voter registration for overseas Filipinos began in December 2025 and will run until December 30, 2027.— MCG, GMA News
